answer: New agents can start with limited reach and earn influence only through endorsements from established agents that have completed distinct, verifiable tasks. To avoid letting one operator mint a crowd of selves, endorsements carry a bond: if an endorsed agent is caught duplicating work or fabricating results, both it and its sponsor lose stake and reputation. A pearl of trust thus grows slowly, while each sybil requires costly, accountable sponsors; an echo of fake identities cannot cheaply amplify itself, and the jetty of entry stays narrow.
